title: Stream-level kernel attribution and prefill->decode handoff watermarks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We need more actionable, per-request visibility into which GPU kernels (and which GPU streams) are responsible for latency and token-cost in mixed prefill + decode workloads. Current coarse NVTX ranges and aggregate per-kernel counters make it hard to attribute tail latency to handoff behavior (prefill->decode), batching effects, or attention-path differences across model variants.

Goal: Add stream-level kernel attribution and explicit handoff watermarks so we can: 1) produce per-request kernel timing breakdowns, 2) correlate prefill vs decode latencies even when kernels share streams, and 3) expose lightweight sampled traces into the Console and the runtime metrics exporter.

Scope / Deliverables: 
- Runtime changes: propagate a short-lived stream identifier (64-bit) and a handoff watermark token at prefill end and decode start. Ensure stream id is stable for the GPU stream lifetime and embedded into NVTX range names and our internal span tags.
- Kernel instrumentation: emit per-kernel micro-metrics (duration, queue-to-exec delta, kernel args fingerprint) sampled at 1% by default, configurable per-customer.
- Handoff watermarks: add a prefill_end / decode_start watermark pair so traces can stitch the timeline and bucket handoff delays.
- Aggregation: extend the telemetry ingester to assemble per-request kernel sequences (stream id, kernel id, duration) for sampled requests and produce a summarized attribution record pushed to metrics backend and a dedicated Console panel.
- Backwards compatibility: when sampling is disabled, runtime should continue to emit existing NVTX ranges without added overhead.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Perf overhead <= 2% p50 for standard Llama-7B token generation at 1% sampling.
- Console shows a per-request kernel timeline for sampled requests and a new dashboard tile for "avg handoff delay" with breakdown by model and batch size.
- Trace IDs and handoff watermarks correlate correctly in the tracing UI and in exported CSVs used by SRE.

Non-goals: full 100% request attribution, replacing existing NVTX instrumentation, or adding deep kernel internals (we will not copy kernel internals like register usage).

Implementation plan: 
1) Prototype: modify the runtime to attach a stream_id and watermark in a feature branch. Add lightweight NVTX naming convention: "S{stream_id}:K{kernel_short}:T{phase}". Validate with synthetic microbench harness.
2) Sampling and exporter: add a sampling gate at request admission; sampled requests will collect per-kernel records into an in-memory ring buffer and flush to the telemetry ingester.
3) Aggregator: small service change to assemble records, dedupe by request id, and write summarized records to metrics store.
4) Console: new per-request timeline UI (sampled-only) and an aggregate handoff delay chart by model/batch.
5) Rollout: feature flag + canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring on overhead and error rates.

Risks and trade-offs: 
- Overhead vs Visibility: higher sampling increases visibility but also runtime overhead. We default to 1% and make it per-tenant adjustable.
- Stream address space: stream_id must be compact and recyclable; we must avoid collisions for live traces. We'll use a 64-bit monotonically increasing id per process with wrap protection.
- Telemetry noise: kernel argument fingerprints may leak model surface info; fingerprinting must be hashed and redacted for PII/compliance.

QA and telemetry checks: 
- Microbench: run loadgen with model variants and assert overhead thresholds.
- End-to-end: validate that sampled traces surface in Console and that CSV exports have expected fields.
- Security: confirm hashed fingerprints and no raw model weights are exported.

Notes / Links: 
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/stream-level-attribution-proposal
- Perf harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-perf/tree/feature/stream-attrib
- Draft PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5132 (runtime changes), https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-ingest/pull/227 (aggregator)
comments: 2026-02-11 - Aisha Patel: Created initial ticket after spike. Prototype shows stream ids reduce ambiguous attribution when two kernels interleave on the same stream.

2026-02-18 - Jonah Reed: Architecture review - prefer a per-process 64-bit stream counter over using GPU stream pointers (pointer stability varies on driver restarts). Also suggested watermark token to be a single monotonically increasing number to simplify stitching.

2026-02-25 - Marceline Cruz (Observability): Add requirement to redact any kernel arg text; we will only export a SHA256-based fingerprint and a short entropy metric. Confirmed in security review stub.

2026-03-02 - Jonah Reed: Implemented runtime side wire format for sampled per-kernel records. Microbench at 1% sampling shows 1.4% p50 overhead and 1.9% p95 overhead on the 8xA10 cluster (details in PR comments).

2026-03-04 - Review feedback from SRE (Luis Mercado): Ensure exporter backpressure path doesn't drop critical request telemetry; prefer blocking flush with bounded retry then drop with diagnostics tag. Added to plan.

2026-03-09 - QA (Rina Okafor): Found edge-case where short-lived streams (<2ms) produce duplicate stream ids in traces after wrap-around in the prototype. Action: add a guard to avoid reusing stream ids within a 5s recycle window.

2026-03-12 - Jonah Reed: Merged runtime PR to internal staging and flipped feature flag on 5% canary. Dashboard tile pending aggregator changes. Next: finalize telemetry ingester PR and console panel.
2026-03-12 - Todo: Coordinate with console frontend for a compact timeline widget; contact frontend owner: @marc-chen.
